description:
# Outcome

One local command creates a complete, tested macOS ARM64 Jido release candidate. The candidate contains a private OTP runtime, a stable archive, checksum, notices, metadata, SBOM when supported, provenance, and acceptance evidence. Its layout and outputs are ready for a later GitHub upload and Homebrew formula.

# Product decision

- Jido has no independent daemon, local protocol, or operating-system service in this release scope.
- TUI, `run`, and `eval` run in the user-started process.
- Use a target-specific Mix release. Burrito is only a fallback for an uncorrectable required failure.
- Preserve fast help and version dispatch and paint-first TUI startup.
- Build macOS ARM64 locally first.
- Do not publish, sign, notarize, or update Homebrew in the active local flow.
- Use `RELEASE_PLAN.md` as the release contract.

# Active local release path

1. `jido_cli-tqg.7.1` — Use an immutable GitHub Jidoka dependency (complete)
2. `jido_cli-tqg.7.2` — Make the Mix application version the only product version source (P0)
3. `jido_cli-tqg.7.12` — Define the local artifact and release metadata contract (P0)
4. `jido_cli-tqg.7.13` — Build the final-archive acceptance harness (P0)
5. `jido_cli-tqg.7.14` — Confirm the source-built Mix release on macOS ARM64 (P0)
6. `jido_cli-tqg.7.15` — Implement the macOS ARM64 private-OTP artifact builder (P0)
7. `jido_cli-tqg.7.16` — Audit shipped dependencies and generate license notices (P1)
8. `jido_cli-tqg.7.17` — Generate local release metadata, checksums, SBOM, and provenance (P1)
9. `jido_cli-tqg.7.18` — Implement one-command local release candidate flow (P0)
10. `jido_cli-tqg.7.19` — Pass automated acceptance on the local release candidate (P1)
11. `jido_cli-tqg.7.20` — Complete manual TUI acceptance on the local release candidate (P1)

The active local release is complete at `jido_cli-tqg.7.20`.

# Later distribution and target work

- `jido_cli-tqg.7.24` — Sign and notarize the macOS ARM64 artifact.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.26` — Publish the accepted artifact to GitHub.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.21` — Publish Jido through the Homebrew tap.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.11` — Prepare Windows launcher and package boundaries.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.25` — Sign future Windows executables.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.27` — Publish a future Scoop manifest.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.28` — Add Linux ARM64.
- `jido_cli-tqg.7.29` — Evaluate Winget and `homebrew/core`.

Homebrew remains in the backlog, but it starts only after the accepted artifact has an immutable GitHub URL.

# Removed from scope

Tasks `7.3` through `7.10`, `7.22`, and `7.23` are closed as removed from scope. They do not represent completed daemon features. They preserve the history of the product decision.

# Dependency map

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  R1["7.1 GitHub dependency"] --> R2["7.2 One version"]
  R2 --> R12["7.12 Artifact contract"]
  R12 --> R13["7.13 Final-archive harness"]
  R12 --> R14["7.14 Confirm Mix release"]
  R12 --> R16["7.16 License inventory"]
  R14 --> R15["7.15 macOS ARM64 builder"]
  R15 --> R17["7.17 Metadata and checksums"]
  R16 --> R17
  R13 --> R18["7.18 One-command local flow"]
  R15 --> R18
  R16 --> R18
  R17 --> R18
  R18 --> R19["7.19 Automated candidate acceptance"]
  R19 --> R20["7.20 Manual TUI acceptance"]
  R20 --> R24["7.24 macOS trust"]
  R24 --> R26["7.26 GitHub publication"]
  R26 --> R21["7.21 Homebrew"]
```

# Gates

- The artifact contract blocks package confirmation and implementation.
- The source-built Mix release blocks the maintained builder.
- Builder, notices, metadata, and the harness block the one-command flow.
- Automated candidate acceptance blocks manual TUI acceptance.
- Manual TUI acceptance completes the current local release goal.
- Signing, GitHub publication, and Homebrew are later, external-state work.
title: Build a local Brew-ready Jido release flow
